pr_title: feat(input): a mode that performs hit target check during input
pr_body:
Reincarnation of #6352.

This change replaces previous `checkHitTarget` heuristic that took place before the action with a new `setupHitTargetInterceptor` that works during the action:
- Before the action we set up capturing listeners on the window.
- During the action we ensure that event target is the element we expect to interact with.
- After the action we clear the listeners.

This should catch the "layout shift" issues where things move between action point calculation and the actual action.

Possible issues:
- **Risk:** `{ trial: true }` might dispatch move events like `mousemove` or `pointerout`,
because we do actually move the mouse but prevent all other events.
- **Timing**: The timing of "hit target check" has moved, so this may affect different web pages
in different ways, for example expose more races. In this case, we should retry the click as before.
- **No risk**: There is still a possibility of mis-targeting with iframes shifting around,
because we only intercept in the target frame. This behavior does not change.

There is an **opt-out** environment variable `PLAYWRIGHT_NO_LAYOUT_SHIFT_CHECK` that reverts to previous behavior.

Fixes #6238.

issue_context.title: [BUG] Wrong element is clicked due to lazy loading/UI shift
issue_context.body:
**Context:**

- Playwright Version: v1.10.0
- Operating System: Mac
- Node.js version: v15.4.0
- Browser: Webkit
- Extra: Docker image - v1.10.0-focal

<!-- CLI to auto-capture this info -->
<!-- npx envinfo --preset playwright -->

**Describe the bug**
Scenario - Click "Contact Agent" button.

Issue - I am trying to click "Contact Agent" button on the page but there is a section "Popular Search" that loads later and shifts the UI. While the test is trying to click the button, the UI changes and instead it ends up clicking one of the popular searches. Please see the screenshot below captured using PWDEBUG=1 - the button is found and highlighted but pointer is on one of the searches.

![webkit_pointer](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22205721/115429903-b81e9b00-a1b8-11eb-9c11-ee80f1c79d5b.png)
comments:
Want to add that we have been able to reproduce this behavior on a site that I am developing browser testing on. The description is very similar to the OP; an optional component of the page loads after the main components have loaded, resulting in the target element shifting down some pixels. Intermittently on CI Playwright clicks on the coordinates where the target _used_ to be, which is now occupied by an entirely different element.

`page.click` nor `elementHandle.click` are able to work around this behavior. Waiting for various load states have also been unsuccessful as the events fire before the delayed element is loaded.

If the team would like logs from my end, please let me know.

> @worldomonation did you try waiting for delayed selector and then clicking the target element?

I have tried various approaches but in my specific encounter with this I was not able to work around it that way. The element that lazy-loads is an optional item that _may_ appear on the site, but not necessarily guaranteed to be present. Think of it as a notice banner that may appear for some accounts but not others.

I'm still in the process of trying to work around the issue, but so far all signs point to either using `waitForTimeout` to let the optional element settle, or introduce some complex switching logic.

Another instance where clicks misses the original element due to the animation/UI shift. Clicking Root opens a dropdown (expanding animation) and after that trying to click `Sign Out` link fails intermittently. Solutions already tried that didn't work:
- `waitForSelector`
- `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`

![wrong_click](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22205721/135020901-e9c34501-fc0a-4fe1-ae10-1d58ab9fc955.JPG)
We have some ideas about addressing this, but did not make it in time for v1.16.

> We have some ideas about addressing this, but did not make it in time for v1.16.

That's great to hear - in the meantime, I have been able to work around this by using page.dispatchEvent("click") on my end.

> We have some ideas about addressing this, but did not make it in time for v1.16.

Thanks. Looking forward to it in v1.17
Since #9546 was reverted, reopening this issue.

I don't think that this is a bug; it is perhaps not even a design flaw, the behaviour just needs to be better documented (maybe in a guide).

Most automaters are used to WebDriver whose [Element.click ](https://www.w3.org/TR/webdriver1/#element-click) operation fires the click event on the target element's parent node.  It appears that Playwright fires the click event much higher up using the _viewport_ XY co-ordinates.  If the element moves between getting the XY co-ordinates and using them (as appears top be the case here), you get a click miss.

There are several solutions to above problem and which one should be used depends on the situation.  You just need to understand that the problem exists before you try and figure out the solution for your situation (you didn't need to worry about this in WebDriver, but I am sure that there is a method to the madness).

@Nav-2d, in the case of the initial problem, the data that is rendered had to come from somewhere and it will usually come in the response to a request that was sent as a result of some event (either an earlier click, or the initial page load).  You just need to figure out which event the request is sent from and do a waitForResponse (it is _rare_ for Web apps to delay rendering after they get a response).

In the case of [your second problem](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/6238#issuecomment-928744966), are you doing `waitForSelector` on the "Sign out" button, or on what ever element is being rendered _after_ the "Sign out" button and causing that button to be pushed down (I am guessing that it is the image)?
